title: Cadence restart handles only the LAST correction; intermediate post-correction cycles get old-cycle labels
detail: corrected_at is one column (the latest stamp) and the latch restarts at most once. With two corrections (correction_cycles is a counter), batches of the first post-correction cycle compare against the SECOND corrected_at, so its re-invitation labels as old-cycle reminder 3+ and only one 'corrected' event renders.
recommended_fix: Track restarts per correction timestamp (or restart when crossing any corrected_at), and emit one 'corrected' entry per cycle — or document single-correction support explicitly.

title: The three preference integration tests are identical in assertions — nothing behavioral distinguishes realtime/daily/off
detail: All three tests assert the same outcome with only the seeded preference string differing — they would all pass if the email gate were removed from maybe_send_email/ maybe_send_rich_email. The pure gate is unit-tested, but the wiring into the dispatch path is behaviorally unpinned.
recommended_fix: Have at least one test observe the email seam per preference (e.g. assert the send path is reached only for realtime), or document why the pure-fn unit test is sufficient for the wiring.

title: Migration comment documents an unconditional updated_at fallback the code does not implement
evidence:
--   terminal statuses — the timeline's "Closed — no reply"-style terminal entry needs
--   a first-class timestamp. The detail read falls back
--   `terminalized_at → submitted_at → objected_at → updated_at` for rows
--   terminalized before this migration.
...
          case normalize_at(taken_over_at) {
            "" -> normalize_at(updated_at)
            _ -> ""
          },
detail: The migration doc states the fallback chain unconditionally, but build_lifecycle_entries skips updated_at when taken_over_at is set (the W2 guard). The in-code comment explains it; the migration comment contradicts it and could mislead future readers.
recommended_fix: Update the migration comment (or the builder doc) to note the taken-over exception: updated_at is only used when the row was never taken over.
